description: C++ Functions, Parameters, Return Values, Default Arguments and Inline Functions

questions.questionText: What is a function in C++?
questions.optionB: A named block of code that performs a specific task
questions.explanation: A function is a named block of code designed to perform a particular task.

questions.questionText: Which part of a function specifies the type of value returned by the function?
questions.explanation: The return type specifies the type of value a function returns.

questions.questionText: Which keyword is used when a function does not return any value?
questions.explanation: The void keyword indicates that a function does not return a value.

questions.questionText: What is a function declaration also commonly called?
questions.explanation: A function declaration is commonly called a function prototype.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is a valid function declaration?
questions.explanation: int add(int, int); is a valid function prototype.

questions.questionText: Which statement is used to send a value back from a function?
questions.explanation: The return statement sends a value back to the calling function.

questions.questionText: What are the values passed to a function when it is called called?
questions.explanation: The actual values supplied during a function call are called arguments.

questions.questionText: What are the variables listed in a function definition that receive values from the caller called?
questions.explanation: Parameters are variables declared in the function definition that receive values from arguments.

questions.questionText: What is the output? int add(int a, int b) { return a + b; } cout << add(3, 4);
questions.explanation: The function returns 3 + 4, which is 7.

questions.questionText: What happens when a void function executes a return statement without a value?
questions.optionC: It always causes a runtime error
questions.explanation: A void function can use return; to exit the function without returning a value.

questions.questionText: Which method passes a copy of an argument to a function?
questions.explanation: In pass by value, a copy of the argument is passed to the function.

questions.questionText: What happens to the original variable when it is passed by value and modified inside the function?
questions.explanation: A separate copy is modified, so the original variable normally remains unchanged.

questions.questionText: Which symbol is used to declare a reference parameter?
questions.explanation: The ampersand (&) is used to declare a reference.

questions.questionText: What is the output? void change(int &x) { x = 20; } int a = 10; change(a); cout << a;
questions.explanation: x is a reference to a, so changing x also changes a to 20.

questions.questionText: What is a default argument in C++?
questions.optionD: A value automatically used when an argument is not supplied
questions.explanation: A default argument provides a value that is used when the caller does not supply that argument.

questions.questionText: Which declaration correctly uses a default argument?
questions.optionB: int add(default int a, int b);
questions.optionC: default int add(int a, int b);
questions.explanation: The declaration int add(int a, int b = 10); gives b a default value of 10.

questions.questionText: What is the output? int add(int a, int b = 5) { return a + b; } cout << add(10);
questions.explanation: Since b is not supplied, its default value 5 is used. Therefore, 10 + 5 = 15.

questions.questionText: Can a C++ function have multiple parameters with default values?
questions.optionB: Only global functions can have them
questions.optionD: Only one parameter can ever have a default
questions.explanation: Multiple parameters can have default values, subject to C++ default-argument rules.

questions.questionText: What is function overloading?
questions.optionA: Using a function inside a loop
questions.optionB: Defining a function without a return type
questions.optionD: Defining multiple functions with the same name but different parameter lists
questions.explanation: Function overloading allows multiple functions to have the same name with different parameter lists.

questions.questionText: Which of the following can be used to distinguish overloaded functions?
questions.explanation: Overloaded functions can differ in the number, types, or order of their parameter types.

questions.questionText: Which keyword can suggest to the compiler that a small function should be expanded at the point of call?
questions.explanation: The inline keyword is used to request inline expansion of a function, although the compiler ultimately decides.

questions.questionText: What is recursion?
questions.explanation: Recursion occurs when a function directly or indirectly calls itself.

questions.questionText: Which part is essential to prevent infinite recursion?
questions.explanation: A base case provides the condition at which recursive calls stop.

questions.questionText: What is the output? int square(int x) { return x * x; } cout << square(5);
questions.explanation: square(5) returns 5 Ã— 5, which is 25.

questions.questionText: What is the output? void show(int x) { cout << x; } show(10);
questions.explanation: The function receives 10 and prints its value.
